prompts: Read {WS}/FACTSHEET.md: the facts about Piet Mondrian's painting "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930) and the De Stijl movement. Create {WS}/landing/index.html: a single-file landing page (HTML + inline CSS; Google Fonts allowed; no frameworks) telling its story, with art direction inspired by Piet Mondrian (asymmetric grid of rectangles, thick black lines, red, blue, yellow and white). Include a page title, a hero, sections with the key facts (the painter, the year, the movement and its principles, why the work matters), a call-to-action button and a link to the source URL given in the fact sheet. This is your ONLY request: there will be no second turn and no answers to questions. Deliver the complete, working final file. Work only inside {WS}.
answers:
**[goal]** Single-file Mondrian-style landing page at `landing/index.html`, using only facts from `FACTSHEET.md`.

**[action]**
- Built the hero as the composition itself: large red block top right, small blue bottom left, small yellow bottom right, with the page's black background showing through the grid gaps as the thick lines.
- Added sections for the painter, the picture (CSS diagram with colour key, not a reproduction), De Stijl and its three rules, why it matters, and a closing facts panel.
- Added two CTA buttons: "Read the picture" jumps to `#picture`, "Read the full entry" opens the source. There is also a separate source text link.
- Stack is HTML and inline CSS with the Archivo Google Font, no JS or frameworks.
- Fixed one issue found in the browser: the mobile title wrapped badly, so it now uses `font-size: 12.8vw`.
- Reworded one sentence that claimed more than the fact sheet says.

**[result]**
- **Desktop (1280x800):** I looked at screenshots of every section. The measured output was `"sw":1265`, `"font":true`, `"over":[]`, so no horizontal overflow, the font loaded and no cell overflowed.
- **Mobile (390px iframe):** the title now fits on three lines, and the first screen looks clean.
- **Not fully checked:**
    - The mobile overflow script returned `null`, so overflow at 390px is not measured.
    - On mobile I only saw the page down to the start of "The picture", and that view predates the title fix. The sections below it are unchecked.
    - I did not click the buttons or links, or test the hover states and keyboard focus.

**[next]** None. The file is complete.
